steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with the gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths of visible light, particularly blue light, are scattered much more efficiently than longer wavelengths like red and yellow, causing blue light to be redirected in all directions across the sky. When you look up, your eyes receive this scattered blue light from every direction, making the entire sky appear blue.
